_meta.title: Era names of the calendars that date the records: Chinese, Japanese, Vietnamese, Western Xia and Korean
_meta.scope: The era and reign names that data/records names or prints, in seven lines. Four of them, zh, ja, vi and xx, are year tables, each along one court's succession; ko, ja-other and zh-other only name the reigns and eras the records print and carry no year.
_meta.yearSpace: Astronomical year numbering, which includes a year 0, so a year N BCE is written as 1 - N.
_meta.fields: lines = one object per line, each with title, scope, line (the succession followed), unit (the English word after the name: reign or era) and eras (the entries, one per line of the file). y = the calendar year this entry takes effect; where a line has year tables the era in force in a year is the last entry with y not greater than that year, and the ordinal year counts from s when present, otherwise from y. s = the year the era itself began, present only when it differs from y. m = the lunar month in which the era takes effect, present only when it is not the first (vi, xx). gap = true means no era is in use from this year until the year given by the next entry. d/dt = dynasty in Simplified and Traditional Chinese. n/nt = era name in Simplified and Traditional Chinese. ja = the Japanese form of the name, present only where it differs from nt (in the ja line it is the name as Japanese writes it today). rom = the Latin-script name the fr, es and it locales print and the en locale prints before the line's unit: toneless pinyin for a Chinese name, Hepburn for a Japanese one, Revised Romanization for a Korean one, quốc ngữ for a Vietnamese one. forms = other spellings of nt that a printed history may set, such as the variant glyph 甯 for 寧, kept as printed. errata = misprints and wrong conversion glyphs found in the base texts, such as 太中祥符 for 大中祥符 and 鹹 for 咸, which a reader's text corrects to nt. A record's supplied token era=<key> names the entry whose rom, lowercased and stripped of diacritics, is the key.
_meta.provenance: Compiled and checked by hand against the standard Chinese, Japanese and Vietnamese calendar concordances; the Vietnamese line from the era names and Chinese cross-reference years printed in the year headings of the Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (Wikisource edition), the Xia line from those of the Xixia Shushi. For 1069-1089 the chronicle and the standard chronology count one year later than some modern lists, and the xx line follows the chronicle. The romanisations come from the build tables of build/lib/era_roman.py and agree with what the translations of the records print. Historical chronology is not itself copyrightable; the choice of the lines, the field design and the transcription are original to this project.

zh.title: Chinese reign eras along a single dynastic line
zh.scope: 330 era names covering 140 BCE to 1911 CE, from Jianyuan to the third year of Xuantong. One era name is given for each year, taken from a single line of succession; contending regimes are omitted.
zh.line: Western Han, Xin, Gengshi, Eastern Han, Wei, Jin, the southern Song, Qi, Liang and Chen, Sui, Tang (with the Wu Zhou interval as Zhou), the Five Dynasties, Song, Yuan, Ming, Qing. The Sixteen Kingdoms, Liao, Jin, Western Xia, the Ten Kingdoms and the Southern Ming are not collected.

zh-other.title: Chinese era names outside the single line
zh-other.scope: Era names and reign names of Chinese regimes that the single line leaves out (Liao, Jin, Northern Wei, Northern Qi, Northern Zhou and others), and the Lu dukes of the Chunqiu, as the translations of the records print them. The list has no year: it names the eras the records use.
zh-other.line: Parallel regimes, in no order; an era name that two regimes bore is one entry.

ko.title: Korean regnal names
ko.scope: The regnal names, Silla titles and posthumous names of the kings of the Korean states that the translations of the records print as a reign. The line has no year: a record's own text fixes the reign, so the entries only name it.
ko.line: Silla, Goguryeo, Baekje, Goryeo and Joseon, in no order; a name that two kings bore is one entry.

ja.title: Japanese era names
ja.scope: 241 entries covering 645 CE to the present, from Taika to Reiwa, of which two mark gaps when no era name was in use. Reckoning runs continuously under one imperial line.
ja.line: A single continuous line with no dynastic divisions. For the period of the two courts, 1331 to 1392, the northern line is followed and the era names of the southern court are not collected.

ja-other.title: Japanese emperors named as a reign
ja-other.scope: The emperors of Japan whose reign the translations of the records print in place of an era name, for the years before eras were in steady use. The line has no year: a record's own text fixes the reign, so the entries only name it.
ja-other.line: Emperors of Japan, in no order.

vi.title: Vietnamese era names along the court line of the Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư
vi.scope: 101 entries from Hưng Thống (989) to Chiêu Thống (1787), the era names the chronicle uses as the running year heading, with gap entries where it names none. Contending regimes are omitted.
vi.line: Former Lê, Lý, Trần (with the Dương Nhật Lễ era Đại Định), the Later Trần, and the Later Lê (Early Lê and Restored Lê as one line). The Hồ, the Mạc, the Tây Sơn, the rebel eras inside these reigns and the Ming occupation years are not collected; gap entries mark 1400–1406, 1414–1427 and 1527–1532, where the chronicle either heads its years with a rival regime or has no Vietnamese era.

xx.title: Western Xia era names as the Xixia Shushi counts them
xx.scope: 27 era names from Tianshou Lifa Yanzuo (1038) to Qianding (1224), the Xia self-eras the chronicle names in its year headings. Each year of the chronicle is headed by a Song era; the Xia era follows it in the first entry of the year.
xx.line: A single line of succession from Jingzong to Modi. The earlier eras Xiandao, Kaiyun, Guangyun and the first Daqing (1032–1037), and the last era Baoyi (1227), are not collected.
